editorial:
Imagine heading back to your old family vacation spot only to find it trashed by squatters. That is exactly what happens to Sarah. She goes back with her dad and uncle to clean the place up and get it ready for the season. The vibe is creepy from the start because they are working in a dark, boarded-up house. As you watch, you feel the tension build up because Sarah keeps hearing strange noises coming from inside the walls. It feels like something is watching them, and you start to wonder if the house is actually haunted or if there is something much worse hiding in the shadows.

What really makes this one work is the big twist that flips everything you thought you knew on its head. The acting is solid, and the way the camera moves keeps you on edge. It does start a bit slow, but the payoff is worth it. If you love a good mystery that keeps you guessing, you should definitely check this out. You can rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night, or if you want the best picture quality, try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to catch all the dark details.
endingExplained: You find out that Sarah is actually dead. She died years ago during a fight with her father. The people you see are not real; they are just parts of her memory. Sarah is a ghost who is stuck in the house, replaying the trauma of her death over and over. The movie ends by showing that she is trapped in a loop of pain and cannot leave the house, making the whole story a sad tragedy.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves twist endings and creepy houses.
